pros: Computes all-pairs shortest paths in a single execution
Simple implementation with clean triple-nested loop structure
Optimal O(V³) for dense graphs (beats V runs of Dijkstra)
Detects negative cycles via diagonal elements
Constant factor is very small (simple min and addition operations)
Naturally produces predecessor matrix for path reconstruction
Well-suited for GPU implementation due to regular memory access
Deterministic execution time (always exactly V³ iterations)
cons: Fixed O(V³) time regardless of graph sparsity
Inefficient for sparse graphs (use Johnson's algorithm instead)
Requires O(V²) memory even for small graphs
Cannot handle graphs with more than ~10⁴ nodes practically
Must process entire matrix even if only few paths needed
No early termination possible (must complete all k iterations)
Floating-point errors can accumulate over many iterations
Overkill when only single-source or single-pair paths needed
Doesn't benefit from graph structure (always V³ operations)
Matrix representation less intuitive than adjacency lists for some
